Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for India's reply to get underway. Michael Bracewell and his men disperse from the huddle and take their respective positions on the field. They are followed by the two Indian openers, Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill. The tall Kyle Jamieson will kickstart proceedings for the visitors. Jamieson to Rohit. Two slips in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

India made good use of the conditions early, with Harshit Rana and Arshdeep Singh striking in their opening overs to leave New Zealand at 5/2. They could not fully capitalise on that start until Rana returned to remove Young, but then Mitchell and Phillips took control as India struggled for answers through the middle. Nitish Kumar Reddy provided some control with an economical spell, and the momentum shifted again when Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep removed the two set batters, helping India pull things back at the death, as at one point, it looked like they would be chasing something over 350. Arshdeep and Rana finished with three wickets each, while Siraj, despite just one wicket, was the most controlled seamer across phases. India now face a challenging chase, but with an unbeaten record at this venue and plenty of quality in their batting, they will fancy their chances. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

One of the two centurions for New Zealand, Glenn Phillips, is in for a chat. Shares that the wicket was a bit two-paced. Feels that it was about building partnerships and as things went on, they managed to find a flow. Mentions that he was a bit itchy around the 30-over mark but Daryl Mitchell took pressure off him. Tells that they were looking at 280 around the 25th over, and he is happy with what they have got on the board. Adds that India bowled well in the middle overs. Shares that Ravindra Jadeja got a couple of balls to hold in the surface and feels the way the Indian bowlers targeted the top of off stump is the way to go for them with the ball.

New Zealand were jolted early with both openers gone for next to nothing, but as has been the pattern this series, Daryl Mitchell stepped in to steady the innings and hold one end firmly. Will Young provided valuable support once again, adding over 50 with Mitchell to revive the innings before departing. With the game still in a delicate phase, Glenn Phillips joined Mitchell and the pair showed remarkable composure, absorbing the pressure before shifting gears. Once set, they took the attack apart, striking boundaries freely and compiling a commanding 219-run stand, with both batters bringing up superb hundreds. Their dismissals briefly slowed the momentum as wickets fell in quick succession, but a late, brisk cameo from Michael Bracewell and a couple of lusty blows by Zakary Foulkes ensured New Zealand pushed comfortably past the 330-mark.

We have witnessed a gripping contest between bat and ball. India struck early and put the Kiwis under pressure, but the BlackCaps responded superbly through the massive Mitchell-Phillips partnership. The Men in Blue, however, fought their way back into the contest towards the end to pull things back slightly. It is hard to judge whether 337 is a strong total on this batting-friendly surface, but New Zealand will take confidence from the fact that in ODIs at this venue, teams batting first have won five times compared to just two wins for sides chasing.

Commentary.Commentary: Time to set the ball rolling in the decider. It is not a full house just yet, but it won't be long before every seat is taken. Mithun Manhas, the president of the BCCI and Mahanaaryaman Rao Scindia, the president of the Madhya Pradesh Cricket Association, do the honours of ringing the bell. Shubman Gill has his men in a huddle near the ropes. Devon Conway and Henry Nicholls walk out to open the innings for New Zealand. A new challenge for the two left-handers with left-arm quick, Arshdeep Singh, in the side today. Arshdeep will open the attack. Conway to face the first ball. Two slips await. Here we go!

The skipper of New Zealand, Michael Bracewell, says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that now they quickly need to shift their mindset to batting first. Mentions that this is a great opportunity for them to win their first ODI series in India. He hopes that the youngsters take their chance and do well. Informs that they are unchanged.

The captain of India, Shubman Gill says that this decider is a great challenge for them as a side and these are the moments you wait for as a player. Feels that there will not be much dew and reckons that this is a pretty good wicket. He believes that it is good to have a total on the board to chase. If India beating New Zealand in the opening ODI came as no surprise, their defeat in Rajkot certainly did. A depleted New Zealand side outplaying a star-studded Indian team was a timely reminder that cricket owes no one guarantees and everything depends on the way you perform on the day.
